Hi Maya — great timing, thanks for sending. Short answers up-front:

- Acceptance criteria: resale certificate needs seller name to match the invoiced entity (Sunridge Wholesale LLC), a valid EIN, purchaser type filled (reseller), a state signature/date or notarization as required by the issuing state, and the ship-to addresses must be covered by a blanket or explicitly listed.
- Blanket coverage: we can map a blanket certificate to multiple ship-to locations if the state allows it and you provide a warehouse matrix that shows which EIN/DBA covers each address.

What I need from you to move this to Finance for validation:
- A signed PDF with the EIN visible on the first page (we can’t accept scans that obscure the EIN).
- The warehouse CSV mapped to the invoiced entity (column header: ship_to_address, city, state, zip, entity_name).
- Confirmation if any of the warehouses are out-of-state for nexus purposes (call out WA vs other states).

I’ll also need a short internal note authorizing application of the certificate to invoices dated back up to 60 days if you want prior-invoice credits. If you want credits applied, confirm the date range.

Looping in Lauren and Monica from finance for the validation step — Lauren / Monica, can you run the acceptance checklist below once Maya confirms the signed files?

Acceptance checklist for Finance:
- Verify seller/invoice entity name match
- Confirm EIN is legible and matches our vendor file
- Confirm certificate state accepts blanket coverage for listed ship-to addresses
- Upload certificate + warehouse matrix to vendor evidence store and tag HubSpot record DL-78412
- If coverage retro is requested, evaluate for invoices within prior 60 days and approve credits per policy

Thanks — if you can get the signed PDF and the corrected CSV today we’ll aim to release any held invoices tomorrow.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
